facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 土_偏财 (Earth carrying The Horizon). Persona The Horizon (偏财). Definition line: "Wide-ranging engagement, opportunity sensed at a distance". Keyword Reach, charge dynamic, poles catalyst Momentum / friction Scatter. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: opportunity sensed far off; the near things blur. Arena: horizon, wind, open road, far light, the next place. Classical portrait: wide-ranging engagement; opportunity sensed at a distance; windfall, generosity, the near things blur. Ruled domains: Opportunity, Ventures, Father. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正财.
Element arena: Earth (ground, soil, load, field, bedrock, harvest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Wood. structural_interaction seed: "Wood directing Earth broadly — reach ranging across stable material".
- k2_overview: "Your Earth moves as the Horizon: ground that acquires. You accumulate opportunity the way land accumulates value, steadily, tangibly, with paperwork. Your ventures have foundations, your windfalls become holdings, and your generosity comes deeded. Fortune trusts you because you give it somewhere to live."
- k2_functional: "You acquire deliberately: surveyed chances, patient closings, ownership that sticks."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Shrewd","Well-traveled","Overflowing"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Opportunity":"Your opportunities are tangible: property, inventory, businesses with floors and keys. You distrust vapor correctly. Walk the ground before buying it, and buy ground more often than promises.","Ventures":"Your ventures should hold weight: real assets, real product, margins you can stack. Compound patiently. In your hands, boring holdings quietly outperform everyone’s exciting stories.","Father":"The father-thread is foundational: a paternal figure tied to property, provision, or their weighty absence. What he built or failed to build shaped your acquiring. Build yours on your own survey."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 土_正财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Thrifty","Steady","Well-stocked"],"friction":["Hoarding","Immobile","Cheap"]}
- Sibling cell 土_正财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Keeping has stopped being a strategy and become a compulsion with a filing system. Money is stored rather than used, and might-need has annexed the garage. Security was the goal once. Now the piles themselves ask for protection, and you provide it nightly."

Core element Wood, energy element Earth. Law: Wood tames Earth (木克土: roots hold the hillside). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Earth is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Wood core that shows Earth on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Earth as the Action is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 木_土's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: The next chance always looks better to you than the one in your hands. Movement is how you feel alive, and you chase what is coming rather than work what is here. You only keep what you stay long enough to collect.

value_b.text: Every new chance pulls at you harder than the one you already took. You need the feeling of a beginning more than a middle, and chasing is how you get it. You chased the one you have now just as hard, and you know it.

value.text: Chasing the next chance costs you the one you hold now. Each new start takes the strength the last one needs, and you would rather begin again than finish. You let the chance in your hands close while you are off chasing.

value.text: You are spread across more things than any one of them can use. Saying no feels like losing, so you hold many small pieces rather than one whole thing. You have every right to say no and give one of them all of you.

value_b.text: Spreading yourself across every venture feels safer to you than trusting one. One thing failing would take you with it, so you keep a piece of everything instead of the whole of anything. Notice that being this spread out keeps you busy rather than safe.

value.text: Spreading yourself thin keeps you from being caught out and keeps you tired. You give each venture enough to stay in rather than enough to win, since quitting feels like losing. You run all of them on the one body you have.

value.text: Starting a thing gives you more than finishing it. The beginning is where the feeling lives, and you spend your strength there rather than on the last stretch. You get nothing for the half until the rest is done.

value_b.text: You start at full strength and finish on what is left. Being new suits you better than being done, and the end asks for strength you spent at the start. Bear in mind how much of the value sits in the part you leave undone.

value.text: Finishing is what you save for later. The last stretch costs you more than the first, and you open a new thing sooner than you close an old one. You leave the money and the credit sitting at the end you skip.
